column1: # CARD_LINEAGE.tsv — the ordered lineage of the frozen V4 task card.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A consumer of a published tape has to answer two
# different questions, and a single hard-coded sha can only answer the first:
#   1. "Am I about to BUILD against the current frozen card?"  -> the card file
#      must hash to the LAST row of this file (the lineage HEAD).
#   2. "Is a tape that was built under an OLDER card still valid?"  -> its
#      `census task_card_v4` sha must be a row of this file, and every
#      amendment AFTER that row must be declared outside the scope the tape
#      constructors actually read.
# The tape read-scope is sections 1..4 plus APPENDIX C4 (tokens S1 S2 S3 S4 C4):
# the walls/roster (S1), the watch and label kernels (S2, S3), the native inputs
# (S4) and the leaf layout (C4). Everything the R2 constructors read lives
# there; S5 onward is the model, which no published byte of a tape depends on.
# An amendment that declares ANY read-scope token retires every earlier tape.
# HONESTY. The scope column is a DECLARATION, and the gate believes it: it is
# the place where a card amendment is claimed to be tape-invariant, and it is
# reviewable against the diff of the two shas. Declaring a read-scope token is
# what turns the gate red for every ancestor, so the declaration is the only
# lever — an under-declared amendment is a falsified record, not a loophole.
# GRAMMAR (enforced by qr::campaign::CardLineage::load, red-fixtured):
#   five tab-separated fields, in file order oldest -> newest, no duplicate sha;
#   sha256    64 lowercase hex characters
#   date      YYYY-MM-DD
#   amendment the change-control id that produced these bytes
#   scope     ROOT (first row only, no predecessor to diff) or a comma list of
#             S1..S9 / C4 naming every card section the diff from the PREVIOUS
#             row touches. An unknown token is a refusal, never a pass.
#   consumers_invariant  what a consumer of an earlier tape may conclude.
sha256
